pages.transcription:
Copy of letter to Jan
Hotel Central                                Rio de Janeiro, 18.Dec. 1940.

Dear Jan,
I have received your letter of Nov. 8th and I have discussed
with Stefan all the questions it involves and immediately made enquiries.
The information which I got from the most competent sources is
that unfortunately there are no chances for a Brazilian visa at the mo-
ment. Besides the capitalist visa - which is out of question as a sum
of ten thousand dollars has to be brought to Brasil - and apart from the
question of the religion they issue now only a few visas for special
technicians and agriculturists which are needed by the Government. -
As to other South American countries, the regulations may vary a little,
but we know from our enquiries for friends that the difficulties as just
as great - for all these countries have now the principle rather to ~~to~~
prevent than to allow immigration. Should the situation change, I would
of course let you know it immediately.
As to financial assistance in the case of your emigration, I
must tell you already now that it is unfortunately impossible for us
to help anybody outside of England, as we have had to leave everything
behind and ourselves living from month to month and from country to
country (we are leaving Brazil in January). In England, however, Stefan
has left with Hanna a certain amount for current expenses in Bath and for
unforeseen payments, and he is writing her not to let you get into
distress.
I can well understand how unhappy you must feel in your present
situation, separated from your wife and unable to find a position, and
I am sorry that there is at present no chance to help you to emigrate
to another counrty. I hope at least that you have good news from your
wife who at any rate is safe from bombing attacks and that you per-
sonally do not suffer too much from the effects of the war. - As to
the past, do not let us talk about it any more, there is for every one
of us plenty to worry about the present time and the future.

With best wishes for the new year and kindest regards,

Dear Hannah, Lotte shows me this letter to her brother. I leave
it quite to you how much you think necessary or advisable
to let him have at once. Only please tell him that this
means no permanent obligation of {our} ~~their~~ part. Any help out
of England is thoroughly excluded as we have ourselves to
renew from month to month our life. [Unterschrift: Stefan]
